paper_title: open university learning analytics dataset
descriptions: The Open University Learning Analytics dataset (OULAD) was developed to support Learning Analytics research by providing a standardized open dataset that links learners’ demographic information with their aggregated clickstream interaction data from the Open University Virtual Learning Environment (VLE). The dataset contains data for 22 module-presentations and 32,593 registered students, including module registrations, assessment results, and VLE interaction logs represented as daily summaries of student clicks (10,655,280 entries). Student demographic attributes are included, and the data were anonymised so that individuals cannot be linked back to identifiable students; quasi-identifying demographic attributes were explicitly identified and generalized using k-anonymity (k=5). The envisioned ML tasks described include predictive modeling of student assessment results and final course results, as well as studying how VLE interactions relate to learning outcomes. The paper does not specify a single required prediction target format across all datasets, but it does outline scenarios for evaluation and model comparison.

paper_title: imagenet large scale visual recognition challenge
official_dataset_name: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) 2010-2014 (classification, single-object localization, and object detection benchmark)
descriptions: The ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge (ILSVRC) is a benchmark for large-scale object category recognition, spanning image classification, single-object localization, and object detection. The paper documents the process of constructing the benchmark by selecting target categories from ImageNet/WordNet, collecting diverse candidate images from the Internet (notably Flickr and search engines), and performing crowdsourced annotation with quality-control pipelines. For classification and localization, images are labeled with the presence/absence of one object category per image (classification) and tight axis-aligned bounding boxes around all visible instances of that category (localization). For detection, images are labeled with the presence/absence of 200 object categories using an efficient hierarchical multi-label question strategy, and then bounding boxes are annotated for every instance with additional verification steps. The primary ML tasks evaluated are categorical image classification (top-5), single-object localization, and object detection (mean average precision).

paper_title: fairface: face attribute dataset for balanced race, gender, and age
descriptions: FairFace is a face image dataset constructed to mitigate race bias in public face attribute datasets by providing more balanced representation across race, gender, and age. It contains 108,501 face images with labels for 7 race groups (White, Black, Indian, East Asian, Southeast Asian, Middle Eastern, Latino), as well as gender and age groups, intended for in-the-wild face attribute classification and cross-dataset evaluation. Faces were collected primarily from the Yahoo YFCC-100M Flickr dataset (with additional sources including Twitter and online newspapers) after detecting faces without preselection, then annotated using human judgments verified via Amazon Mechanical Turk workers with agreement/republication logic and further refinement using model predictions plus manual re-verification. The paper’s ML task is supervised classification of face attributes (race, gender, and age) and evaluation of generalization and balanced accuracy across subpopulations.

paper_title: natural adversarial examples
descriptions: IMAGENET-A is a curated dataset of real-world natural adversarially filtered images intended to reliably degrade ImageNet image classification models under distribution shift. It contains images from a selected 200-class subset of ImageNet-1K, where the images are filtered so that they are misclassified by a ResNet-50 model (and the resulting mistakes transfer to other architectures). The paper describes how candidates are collected from other web sources, then removed if they are correctly classified by ResNet-50 (including crop-based filtering and a confidence threshold), followed by a second filtering stage to control error confusions, and finally manual selection by graduate students to ensure visual clarity and single-label validity. The envisioned ML task is image classification robustness evaluation (top-1 accuracy) under natural adversarial shifts, and the paper also evaluates calibration/uncertainty and error detection metrics using this dataset.

paper_title: d4rl: datasets for deep data-driven reinforcement learning
official_dataset_name: D4RL (Datasets for Deep Data-Driven Reinforcement Learning) benchmark suite
descriptions: The paper introduces D4RL, a benchmark suite of tasks paired with pre-collected offline reinforcement learning datasets, specifically designed to study offline RL under conditions motivated by real-world data collection. It includes multiple simulated domains (e.g., Maze2D, AntMaze, Gym-MuJoCo, Adroit, FrankaKitchen, Flow, and CARLA offline CARLA tasks) with datasets generated via distinct data-collection procedures such as hand-designed controllers, human demonstrations, imitation-cloned policies, and mixtures of policies. The data is provided as fixed sets of trajectory transitions (state/action/next-state/reward) used for training offline RL algorithms, and each dataset is evaluated in simulation with a standardized evaluation protocol (training vs evaluation task splits and normalized scores). The intended ML task is offline reinforcement learning: learning a policy from a fixed dataset to maximize discounted returns, with difficulty factors such as narrow/biased distributions, sparse rewards, partial observability, and undirected/multitask data (stitching).

paper_title: superglue: a stickier benchmark for general-purpose language understanding systems
descriptions: SuperGLUE is a benchmark designed to provide a simple, robust evaluation metric for general-purpose English language understanding systems. It consists of a public leaderboard built around eight language understanding tasks (BoolQ, CB, COPA, MultiRC, ReCoRD, RTE, WiC, WSC) with a single-number performance score and an analysis toolkit. The paper describes human performance estimation via crowd-sourced annotation (two-step training then annotation with majority vote) and includes additional diagnostic datasets (an expert-constructed diagnostic set from GLUE and Winogender) with separate scoring; the task-level labels are not demographic attributes, but the Winogender diagnostic is explicitly used to analyze gender bias in coreference. paper_title: a broad-coverage challenge corpus for sentence understanding through inference
descriptions: MultiNLI is a dataset introduced for training and evaluating machine learning models for sentence understanding using natural language inference (NLI), also known as recognizing textual entailment. It provides labeled sentence pairs (premise, hypothesis) with genre coverage from ten distinct genres spanning written and spoken English; the paper frames this as remedying SNLI’s single-genre image-caption limitation and enabling cross-genre domain adaptation evaluation. Each example includes premise/hypothesis strings plus parsing fields and per-annotator validation labels for development/test splits, and the envisioned ML task is 3-way NLI classification.

paper_title: learning de-biased representations with biased representations
descriptions: Biased MNIST is a synthetic dataset constructed by modifying the standard MNIST digits to introduce a background color bias that correlates with the digit label during training. Each digit image is assigned one of 10 pre-selected background colors, where the correct (label-dependent) color is chosen with probability ρ and an incorrect color is chosen with probability 1−ρ, so ρ controls the strength of the bias. descriptions: The dataset consists of tweets and the derived follower-based social graph of Twitter users who posted messages related to the Higgs boson discovery. The authors collect tweets posted between 00:00 AM on 1 July 2012 and 11:59 PM on 7 July 2012 containing at least one of the keywords/hashtags: lhc, cern, boson, higgs. For each tweet, the paper uses the user’s profile Location field when available to assign a geographic position, producing a subset of geo-located tweets. The dataset is used to study information spreading and rumor dynamics on Twitter—reporting macroscopic spatio-temporal patterns and modeling activation/de-activation dynamics on the constructed network. The paper does not describe any additional per-tweet or per-user human labeling process beyond the keyword-based inclusion criteria and the derived geo-position when Location is present.
